docs/QUALITY_BAR.md gap D. The project already decided Unity's own Scene-view Move/Rotate/Scale tools replace devmode.js's TransformControls gizmo outright ('the editor IS the gizmo') — correct for the gizmo itself, but devmode.js ALSO persists per-object position overrides to localStorage, re-applies them on load, and prints a copyable snippet, which is real functionality with no Unity-editor equivalent until this file. DevPlacement.cs (359 lines, Assets/Editor/ — uses UnityEditor APIs throughout) ports: the opt-in registry with the 'baked-collider props must not register' rule (devmode.js's own example: the tables/ranges, whose colliders are baked into a world-space soup keyed by where the code placed the mesh); EditorPrefs persistence as ONE JSON blob under one key (Newtonsoft JsonConvert, the same library CityMaterials.cs already depends on) — the direct structural analogue of devmode.js's single `tf-dev-overrides` localStorage key, including the same per-machine/non-portable trade-off the JS already had; re-application from THREE separate hooks (EditorSceneManager.sceneOpened, AssemblyReloadEvents.afterAssemblyReload, and an EditorApplication.update poll for anything registering afterward) specifically because devmode.js's own header flags a 'reload-lands-on-menu' class of bug — an object silently not reapplying its saved spot after a reload reads as a vanished edit, so this errs toward redundant re-apply paths rather than one; the copyable snippet (devmode.js:242-255) including WORLD position/yaw and lat/lon via GeoFrame.ToLatLon (Assets/Scripts/Data/GeoFrame.cs — read, not edited); and the pointer-guard (devmode.js's CLICK_PX: a press that travels less than 4px is a click, not a drag) reproduced as an epsilon guard (POS_EPS/ROT_EPS/SCALE_EPS) on the auto-commit poll, since Unity's built-in gizmo has no generic 'drag ended' event for an arbitrary registered object the way three.js's TransformControls fires 'dragging-changed' — diffing against the last-committed TRS each editor tick reproduces the same end state ('every drag is saved') without one. DevPlacementTag.cs (47 lines) is the MonoBehaviour a prop attaches to opt in — deliberately placed OUTSIDE Assets/Editor/ (a component meant to live on a scene GameObject cannot sit in a folder Unity treats as editor-only; its calls into DevPlacement are #if UNITY_EDITOR-guarded, compiling to an inert tag in a player build). NOT PORTED, by the project's own prior decision: the translate/rotate/scale mode buttons, snap toggle, world/local toggle, the in-game panel UI, the ` hotkey and click-to-select raycast — all replaced wholesale by Unity's native Scene view, which already has every one of those as a first-class feature. (357 lines)

PROBE BUG, not a port bug (and the real numbers were already verified; only the probe's VERDICT was wrong). tools/_probe_crashmath.mjs prints 26 lines: 8 CRASHM lines (5 cross + 3 reflect, mback_*/side_* or r_*) that DO have a CrashProbe.cs counterpart, and 18 CRASHM_CHECK lines (3 per cross id x5 + 1 per reflect id x3: handWrittenIsCross/swapMatches/unswappedIsNegative/mirrorInvariant) that are the JS script's OWN self-verification of its hand-written formula — proving src/crash.js:130's `new THREE.Vector3(-back.z,0,back.x)` really is algebraically back.cross(up), using THREE's own cross()/reflect(), with no Unity involved. These 18 lines lacked the tools/unity_port_check.py JSONLY prefix convention (its one_sided() check), so every one counted as an unmatched js-only line and pushed the probe to FAIL (12 shown, all 'no C# line matching') even though the 8 real CRASHM pairs (39 values) matched CS to 0.000e+00 relative difference, both before and after this fix — the FEED-style numeric drift never existed here. Investigated whether the 3-line shape belongs on the C# side (the task's stated preference) and found a concrete reason it cannot be: Core/CrashSequence.cs:194 calls `Vector3.Cross(Vector3.up, back)` directly and carries no second, independently hand-written cross formula to re-derive against — porting 'handWrittenIsCross' etc. to C# would mean inventing a redundant hand-rolled cross just to prove it equals Vector3.Cross, testing the test rather than the port. Fixed on the JS side instead: the check() helper now prints `JSONLY CRASHM_CHECK ...` (one line changed, tools/_probe_crashmath.mjs's check() function), which tools/unity_port_check.py already treats as a by-design one-sided fact (counted, never paired, no longer a failure). Verified: `python3 tools/unity_port_check.py` now reports 'compared 39 values across 8 js / 8 cs lines ... one-sided facts not paired (by design): 18 js, 0 cs ... PASS - 39 values match to float32 precision' (was FAIL before, same 39/39 match underneath). tools/_probe_crashmath.mjs

PROBE BUG, not a port bug. The 7e-4 FEED drift (js=0.01353 cs=0.01352) traced to its source: tools/_probe_damage.mjs's FEED/BRIDGE/JOIN sections built their own local stand-in cartridges (pistolCart={bullet:9.02,energy:580}, akmCart={bullet:7.92,energy:2000}, bellyCart={bullet:12.7,energy:16000}) instead of importing the real CARTRIDGES table from src/ballistics.js:78-133. DamageProbe.cs's FeedGrowthFacts()/BridgeAndJoinFacts() correctly read Cartridges.Para9x19/M43_762x39/Heavy127x108 from the REAL ported Combat/Ballistics.cs (bullet 9.01/7.92/12.98 mm, energy 580.6/2019.3/16238.5 J — derived via 0.5*m*v0^2, not literals). So the two sides disagreed on INPUT (9.02mm vs the real 9.01mm bullet diameter), not on arithmetic: tearRadius(cal,1)=1.5*cal amplified the 0.01mm input difference into the 7e-4 relative drift on r. None of the three float-precision causes named in the unity skill (fract-hash double, accumulator, Mathf.RoundToInt-vs-Math.round) applied — ruled out by tracing cal/r by hand on both sides before touching any code. Fix: tools/_probe_damage.mjs now imports { CARTRIDGES } from '../src/ballistics.js' and uses CARTRIDGES['9x19']/['7.62x39']/['12.7x108'] in place of the three stand-in literals (both the FEED block and the BRIDGE/JOIN loop). This also silently fixed BRIDGE/JOIN's own pre-existing input mismatch (belly bulletMm 12.7 vs the real 12.98 was the worst, rel=2.16e-2) which the 12-mismatch display cap in tools/unity_port_check.py had been hiding behind the FEED failures. After the fix: FEED and BRIDGE/JOIN lines match CS to float32 precision (0 relative difference at the printed precision). Residual, OUT-OF-SCOPE float noise still present in the same probe pair (TEARRADIUS id=762x39_n2/127x108_n2, ~3-5e-5 relative, just over the 1e-5 tolerance, likely Mathf.Pow(1f,0.6f) vs Math.pow(1,0.6) base-1 special-casing; GLASS id=shatter steps=50 vs 49, an off-by-one rest-frame threshold crossing; BREAKWALL id=crumble 3.3e-4) was NOT touched — it predates this fix, was masked by the same 12-entry cap, and is unrelated to the FEED/cartridge bug this task scoped. Flagging it as an honest open item rather than silently leaving it. tools/_probe_damage.mjs

HOW THE PANEL IS CAPTURED, since this was the hard part: a screen-space-overlay panel is NOT drawn by Camera.Render() into a RenderTexture - URP gates overlay UI on UniversalCameraData.rendersOverlayUI = rendersUIOverlay && resolveToScreen, and resolveToScreen is `targetTexture == null` (UniversalCameraData.cs:307,384), so pointing the camera at a target texture silently drops the whole UI with every 'UI installed' flag still true. What works is PanelSettings.targetTexture (makes it an OFFSCREEN panel) plus a hand-driven repaint, because edit mode has no player loop: UnityEngine.UIElements.UIElementsRuntimeUtility's internal UpdatePanels() + RepaintPanels() + RenderOffscreenPanels() by reflection. That is the path that produced pixels (UIRENDER path=runtimeUtility, 2,073,600 non-transparent px on the full-screen shell); the fallback path (the panel object's own Update()/Repaint(Event)) was never needed. The target is ARGB32 + RenderTextureReadWrite.sRGB so GetPixels32 hands back the final display bytes, directly comparable with the hex. The panel MUST be pinned to that target before anything is measured: with no target texture a panel lays out at Screen.width x Screen.height, which is 640x480 in batch mode, and every worldBound would be in a different space from the pixels. style.css

CONFIRMED, NOT FIXED — root cause is upstream of this file and the real fix is out of this task's safe scope; reporting per the task brief's instruction to STOP and report a confirmed site that traces back to shared foundational data, the same category as Data/GeoFrame.cs/Data/TerrainSampler.cs.

FacadeRelief.BuildFacade's window-placement loop (FacadeRelief.cs:129-184, porting citymap.js:4893-4907 (the `us[]` perimeter-UV accumulation) and citymap.js:5064-5080 (the window-column walk `for (let k = Math.ceil(u0+0.5)-0.5; k+0.5<=u1; k+=1)`)) computes `perim`, `us[]`, `len`, and the loop variable `k` as `float`/`Mathf.Sqrt`, where citymap.js uses `Math.hypot` and has no float32 at all (double throughout). This is the exact shape of the two bugs already fixed project-wide (ParkBuilder's path-furniture walk, RiverSheet's triangulator): an accumulator/threshold comparison whose last-iteration flip depends on float32 vs float64 rounding.

PROOF, run against the REAL building dataset (public/tbilisi/city.json.gz, 193146 buildings, 849135 wall segments with len>=5): reimplementing the us[]-accumulation + window-column loop twice in Node — once plain double, once with every operation passed through Math.fround (emulating C#'s float) — gives:
  float64 (matches citymap.js):  totalWinCols=3291565  segsChecked(len>=5)=849135
  float32 (matches current C#):  totalWinCols=3291406  segsChecked(len>=5)=849117
  delta: -159 window columns city-wide, and 18 segments flip the `len<5` corner-skip gate — both deltas are small, mixed-magnitude, and only visible per-segment (never on a single building), exactly the 'parks' signature.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART, per the river lesson ('precision must be carried from the SOURCE, not restored at the point of comparison'): widening FacadeRelief.cs's own arithmetic to double would NOT fix this. `contour` (FacadeRelief.BuildFacade's `float[] contour` parameter) is `BuildingBuilder.cs`'s `e.Flat`, which traces back to `Data/CityData.cs:150` (`ReadFootprints`): `buf.Add(Convert.ToSingle(jr.Value))` followed by `flat[i-1] = buf[i]/10f` — the building contour coordinates are rounded to float32 at JSON-PARSE time, before any geometry math runs at all. Proven directly: re-running the same Node simulation with coordinates pre-rounded through Math.fround ONLY at parse time, but every subsequent arithmetic op kept in double (i.e. 'widen the math, not the source'), reproduces the CURRENT (wrong) float32 numbers EXACTLY (totalWinCols=3291406, segsChecked=849117) — identical to doing everything in float32. There is nothing left to recover downstream once the source is rounded.

WHY NOT FIXED HERE: the real fix is widening `Data/CityData.cs`'s `Footprint.Flat` (declared `public float[] Flat`, City/CityData.cs:39) to `double[]`, carried as double through `BuildingBuilder.cs`'s `e.Flat`/`FacadeRelief.cs`'s `contour` all the way to the window/balcony/cornice loops, narrowing to float only at the `GeoFrame.ToUnity(...)` call sites. `Footprint.Flat` is read by at least 9 other City/ builders (BuildingBuilder.cs, BuildingParts.cs, ShopfrontBuilder.cs, PhotoFacades.cs, SpawnFinder.cs, VegetationLoader.cs, RoadSignsStreetlights.cs, Core/CombatBuildingChunk.cs, Combat/BreakWall.cs) beyond FacadeRelief.cs itself, and by two files another agent currently owns (City/CityLoader.cs, City/BridgeBuilder.cs, both of which reference `.Flat`). Changing this shared data contract carries exactly the blast-radius risk the task brief calls out for Data/GeoFrame.cs/Data/TerrainSampler.cs ('Shared by every builder; a change there silently moves the whole city') even though CityData.cs is not literally named in that exclusion — the same caution applies by the brief's own stated principle, and editing it risks breaking the two excluded in-flight files. Reporting for a decision rather than fixing.

Scale note: 159 window columns out of 3.29M is a ~0.005% delta — small relative to the whole city, same order as the trees +110/46627 (+0.24%) delta the parks fix closed — but it is NOT the only consumer of Footprint.Flat's float32 rounding; BuildingBuilder.cs's own roof/wall vertex writes, BuildingParts.cs's OSM-3D-parts extrusion, and every other Flat-reading builder listed above inherit the same source-precision loss and were NOT individually re-audited here (out of scope for this pass — this entry is about FacadeRelief.cs's window/balcony/cornice loop specifically, where the divergence was proven).

(2) 'arithmetic widened to double, coordinates pre-rounded to float32 at parse time' run -> reproduces the float32 numbers EXACTLY (3291406 / 849117), proving the fix must be upstream at Data/CityData.cs's Footprint.Flat, not inside FacadeRelief.cs. units.note: NEW FILE, claims 0 lines -- it ports no JS, it fixes a port defect. Shared clear for the city's 'nothing is baked, OnEnable -> EnsureBuilt regenerates' contract. MEASURED DEFECT: every scenery renderer is [ExecuteAlways] with OnEnable -> EnsureBuilt, but only ShopfrontRenderer.ClearChildren walked real Transform children. ParkRenderer's and LandmarkRenderer's cleared a private List<GameObject> _children -- a private field is not serialised, so a SCENE LOAD leaves it empty while the deserialised children are right there -- and MetroRenderer, MallRenderer and StreetFurnitureRenderer had no clear at all. The baked copies therefore survived the load and the fresh build was added alongside them: the Buildings root held 2,735 descendants after loading the baked scene against 1,771 after loading a stripped one, ~964 objects co-located and drawn twice, with 2.50 GB peak load memory. GeneratedChildren.Clear(root, disposeRuntimeAssets) destroys every real Transform child (ShopfrontRenderer's pattern, plain DestroyImmediate in edit mode, never Undo.DestroyObjectImmediate -- an undo record per object is pointless for regenerated geometry) and optionally reclaims the non-persistent Meshes/Materials/Texture2Ds those children referenced, skipping anything EditorUtility.IsPersistent owns so it can never eat an imported FBX/OBJ asset. All eight renderers call it: Park/Landmark/Mall with disposal (per-build meshes, MatLambert/MatWater/clamped-clone materials, 42 rasterised 1024x128 mall sign plates), Shopfront without (bit-for-bit its old behaviour; SignPool owns its slots), Metro without (its _matCache and _nameBoardMesh are static, built once per domain -- and both were hardened to tolerate a destroyed object: `&& hit != null` on the three _matCache lookups and `if (_nameBoardMesh == null)` instead of `??=`, because C#'s null-coalescing does not see Unity's destroyed-object null and would return a corpse forever), and City/Vegetation/StreetFurniture as insurance -- those three create ZERO Transform children (everything is a Matrix4x4 in _batches) so they were never part of the double-draw, but a private _batches guard means a load always re-enters EnsureBuilt and the uniform contract is the only defence against a future child-creating pass. Each renderer also gained an internal RebuildForCheck() that clears its build guard (and empties _children WITHOUT destroying, reproducing a fresh component) and re-runs EnsureBuilt. PROVEN by Editor/SceneryRebuildCheck.cs against the real Assets/Scenes/Game.unity: pass1==pass2 for all eight (City 0/0, Shopfront 195/195, Vegetation 0/0, Park 224/224, Metro 557/557, Mall 84/84, StreetFurniture 0/0, Landmark 96/96), REBUILDCHECK_RESULT checked=8 doubled=0, and every renderer's own count line repeats identically on the second build (METRORENDERER spawned=106, MALLRENDERER spawned=84). The harness is NOT vacuous: a one-file negative control restoring ParkRenderer's old _children-list clear made it report park 224 -> 448 ok=false, doubled=1, exit 1, and was reverted immediately.

units.note: NOT new coverage — a numeric-precision fix to the already-ported _buildRiverSheet triangulation (citymap.js:7373-7614, river.json:591-677), closing the open RiverProbe vs tools/_probe_river.py count/area mismatch (C# 157559 verts/244112 tris/area 6569212 m^2 vs the reference 157547/244096/6569580). Root causes are TWO, independent, and were conflated before this fix: (1) COUNT (+12 verts/+16 tris): EarClip.Triangulate (citymap.js's THREE.ShapeUtils.triangulateShape equivalent, hand-rolled since Unity ships no earcut) is precision-sensitive near-degenerate is-ear/point-in-triangle cross-products, and citymap.js's own numbers (and _probe_river.py's) are always 64-bit JS/Python floats, never float32. The port stored ring coordinates in UnityEngine.Vector2 (32-bit) from JSON-parse time onward, losing bits BEFORE any triangulation math ran. Added per-ring 'RIVERP ringdbg' diagnostics to both RiverProbe.cs and _probe_river.py (merged-ring length + pre-subdivision triangle count per outer, printed before/after the 2 quad-subdivision passes) and diffed all 76 used rings: only ring i=6 (27 holes bridged into one 2399-point outer, the densest real ring) disagreed — pretris 1790 (C#) vs 1789 (Python) — every other ring matched exactly. First attempted fix (widen only the Cross/IsReflex/PointInTri arithmetic inside Triangulate to double, keeping Vector2 storage) did NOT change the result: the coordinates were already float32-rounded at parse time, so there was nothing left to recover by computing in double afterward. The real fix is RiverSheet.Vec2D, a new double-precision point struct that carries ring coordinates from ReadRing through Poly/RingRec/EarClip.MergeHoles/EarClip.Triangulate unrounded, converting to float only once, at Mesh/UV/Bank write time where float32 genuinely suffices. After the fix ring i=6 matches (pretris 1789, fverts 18917, ftris 28624, identical to Python) and so does the citywide total (157547/244096, exact). (2) AREA (368 m^2 gap, independent of the count bug): RiverSheet.BuildSheetAndBanks summed per-triangle shoelace area into a 32-bit `float` accumulator (`float area2`) over 244,112 terms; tools/_probe_river.py's `total_area = sum(...)` is a plain Python float, always 64-bit, with no such accumulation error. Changed the accumulator to `double`, casting to float only at SheetAreaM2's assignment. Verified together: after both fixes, `python3 tools/unity_port_check.py /tmp/river_js.txt <RiverProbe log>` reports PASS, 597 values matched, worst relative difference 2.794e-06 (float32 display rounding on an unrelated bed-height sample, not a regression), 0 js-only unmatched lines. WaterBodies.cs (a separate, shared consumer of RiverSheet.EarClip.Triangulate for lake contours, owned by another unit) was not touched: EarClip gained a Vector2-taking overload that forwards into the new double-precision one, so its existing call compiles and behaves unchanged (lake triangulation has no holes/bridging and was never shown to need the extra precision — this fix did not touch or re-verify WaterBodies' own numbers). RiverSheet's public surface (Build, HeightAt, LevelAt, MeasuredLevelAt, InRiverMask, RiverDepth, Mesh, Banks, all diagnostic counts) is unchanged; Vec2D and the new per-ring RingDebug list are additive.

CONFIRMED and FIXED: BreakWall.WriteShellVerts (BreakWall.cs:342-344, porting src/breakwall.js:282-284's writeShellVerts) called the double-precision sin-fract hash `Fr(double v)` (BreakWall.cs:322, itself correctly double) with float-SUFFIXED multiplier literals — `Fr(v * 12.9898f + phase * 7.31f)`, `Fr(v * 78.233f + phase * 3.17f)`, `Fr(v * 39.425f + phase * 5.53f)` — where `v` is the `int` vertex-loop index (`for (int v = 0; v < s.Count; v++)`, BreakWall.cs:333). The `f` suffix forces `int * float = float` arithmetic BEFORE the result widens to `double` at the call boundary, which is exactly the failure mode this project's own BuildingDamage.Fr doc comment (City/BuildingDamage.cs:216-219) names verbatim: "computing v * 12.9898f in float32 first and widening afterwards reintroduces the same error one step earlier." BuildingDamage.WriteBuildingVerts (the sibling intact-building crumble path breakwall.cs's own comment cites as 'the same damage math the intact shells use') gets this right with unsuffixed literals (`Fr(v * 12.9898 + phase * 7.31)`, City/BuildingDamage.cs:254) — BreakWall.cs is the one site that regressed it when porting writeShellVerts for BROKEN (carved-open) building shells.

This is the sin*43758.5453 hash the project has already proven is pathologically precision-sensitive (BuildingDamage.cs's own measured example: at v=1000, float64 gives 0.943384, float32 gives 0.474609 — a different random number, not a rounding error, moving a vertex 1.15 m). Unlike that documented case (world-space px/pz reaching ~3.4e6), here `v` is a small vertex index, but the magnitude of the resulting hash disagreement does not depend on v being large — it is a chaotic function of the argument's low-order bits, which float32 rounds away almost everywhere, not just past some threshold.

PROOF (Node, reimplementing both argument paths exactly: float32 arg via Math.fround on every op vs. the plain double formula, for v=0..4999, phase=0): 4497 of 5000 vertex indices (90%) disagreed by >0.05 between the two hash outputs, worst case 0.996 (i.e. opposite ends of the 0-1 range) — not a rare edge case, the DOMINANT case. Every crumbled/broken building wall's per-vertex jitter position (src/breakwall.js:282-284's px/py/pz) was therefore wrong on roughly 9 in 10 vertices whenever a wall took blast damage and the shell was re-written, which happens on every hit (BreakWall.Carve -> WriteShellVerts is called per building per damage tick, not once).

FIX: removed the `f` suffix from all 6 literals (12.9898, 78.233, 39.425, 7.31, 3.17, 5.53) in the three Fr(...) call expressions, matching BuildingDamage.cs's own unsuffixed convention exactly. `int v * double-literal` now promotes to double per C# numeric-promotion rules, so the full `v*mult + phase*mult2` expression is computed in double before Fr(double) ever sees it — identical to src/breakwall.js (JS has no float32 at all, so this was always double there). No other change: Fr's own body, the per-vertex jit/t/a/relY math, and the lining-vertex loop (which has no hash call) are untouched.

NOT a new finding about CityData/Footprint.Flat's float32 origin (see the sibling precision.json entry below) — s.OrigP here is a Vector3[] already materialized per-building at shell-build time; v is a loop counter, not a coordinate, so there is no upstream-float32-source issue for THIS particular bug — narrowing the argument expression's own arithmetic is sufficient and complete.

MEASURED DEFECT (docs/open_items.json `spawn-in-building`): Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs placed the player's aeroplane at the DATA ORIGIN (new Vector3(0, groundY + 15, 0)), and the origin is Delisi, mid-block -- not on the avenue. Measured from the first GPU render: plane y=492.09 (terrain 477.09 + 15), bounds 490.94..495.70, and a downward ray hit collider=chunk_18 root=Buildings at y=494.64, i.e. a BUILDING SURFACE PASSED THROUGH THE AIRFRAME on frame one; scratchpad/shots/heroplane_top.png showed a roof where the plane should be. src/citymap.js:6484-6531 `_computeSpawn` has no such problem because the JS SEARCHES the real road network at load time for the nearest avenue (width >= 8 m) and snaps the spawn onto it; SpawnFinder.cs is a complete, faithful port of that search and `grep -rn SpawnFinder unity/Assets/Scripts` returned NOTHING -- its only caller anywhere was Editor/Probes/CityGeoProbe.cs. This file loads the same merged network every other runtime consumer loads (City/VegetationRenderer.cs:200-206 and City/StreetFurnitureRenderer.cs:168-174 verbatim: legacy packed lists out of city.json.gz, roadnet.json.gz merged over the top inside citymap.js:539-541's own try/catch), runs SpawnFinder over it, caches the answer for the session, and converts the GAME-frame result to the Unity transform GameLoop applies. THE YAW IS NOT JUST GeoFrame.YawToUnity, and the file carries the derivation: SpawnFinder returns `atan2(-fx,-fz)`, the Y rotation for an object whose nose is its own -Z (src/planes.js straightens every airframe to -Z), while this port's planeRoot is NOSE = +Z because Flight/PlaneModelFrame.cs absorbed that 180 degrees in `model_frame`. A naive YawToUnity therefore points the aeroplane down the road BACKWARDS -- ENE instead of WSW. yawUnity = atan2(-noseGameX, noseGameZ) = PI - yawGame, written as the two-line vector derivation so the reason survives. MEASURED on the shipped scene (Editor/Probes/CoreSpawnProbe.cs): SPAWNRESOLVER source=road found=true roads=56259 gameXZ=(4.30,30.40) yawGame=-1.4165 yawUnity=-1.7251 roadWidth=22.2m -- a 22.2 m avenue 30 m from the origin, which is Vazha-Pshavela, and SPAWN_YAW dot=1.0000 between the plane's actual forward and the mirrored road heading, legacyDot=0.9847 (citymap.js:6520-6529's WSW side).

NEW FILE, claims 0 lines -- it ports no JS, it makes the hero's starter plane actually reach the one PlaneController the scene has. WHY NOT 35 CONTROLLERS: one aeroplane is flyable at a time and a PlaneController carries a whole flight rig (FlightModel, PlaneRaycastWorld, ground probe, ground roll, hull damage, wall contact, plane physics); 35 of those for one flown machine is the opposite of this port's perf history. The shape reused is the Enter-takes-a-parked-plane path (GameLoop.SwapToPlane -> PlaneController.Init -> PlaneModelFrame.Ensure). Order, and every step of it is load-bearing: the old `model_frame` is DETACHED before it is destroyed (Object.Destroy is deferred to end of frame and transform.Find still returns a Destroy()'d object until then, so PlaneModelFrame.Of would have handed Attach a corpse) -- and one detach takes the cockpit kit, the hinged hood and the measured box shell with it, because PlaneCockpitBaker builds all three under the measure frame; PlanePropellers is DestroyImmediate'd, since it caches blade transforms inside the model that just went and its `_built` flag is private with no reset, and PlaneController.Init's own `GetComponent<PlanePropellers>() == null` test runs in the same frame (a jet must not inherit the Mustang's blur disc); Attach, not Ensure, applies def.Scale and src/planes.js:834's orientation fix for the NEW airframe; PlaneCockpitBaker.Bake re-measures the cockpit/shell for it (the same call Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs makes, flyable:true); PlaneDamageRecord is rederived by Flight/PlaneHallFill.cs:341-356's own formulae (planes.js:1574/1575/1587 off the identity-measured box, +max.z for the nose since this frame's nose is +Z, Planes.PlaneStamina from target.js:69); and PlaneController.ReInit rebuilds the flight rig from the new row. The gun pod is deliberately LEFT -- it hangs on the flight root, not the model, and Combat/GunPod's muzzleLocal is a constant. Asset resolution is AssetDatabase, Editor-only, the established convention for every model in this port (PlaneHallFill loads all 35 the same way); in a player build or on a missing asset the hero keeps the baked machine rather than flying an invisible one.

THE BIGGEST VISIBLE BUG (docs/QUALITY_BAR.md) closed: the aeroplane the player flies no longer points its tail along the thrust vector. covers:0 BY ARITHMETIC, not by modesty -- src/planes.js is at 1614/1614 claimed, 0 free, so src/planes.js:813-836 makePlaneModel's straightening tail and :1528-1540 makeGameplayPlane's wrapper/group nesting are reported in prose here rather than billed. Nothing in this entry adds a line of coverage; it makes already-billed lines actually RUN, which is this port's signature failure mode.

WHAT WAS WRONG. PlaneDef.YawUnity/RollUnity had zero Transform consumers and the model child was parented at IDENTITY in all four places a plane gets built, so (a) the straightened nose stayed on -Z while Flight/FlightModel.cs thrusts along plane.forward = +Z, and (b) the 9 defs that carry an orientation fix were never straightened at all.

THE FIX IS ONE CHAIN, THREE NODES, because three different frames are genuinely needed and collapsing any two re-creates the bug:
  planeRoot            FLIGHT frame, nose +Z (FlightModel, Combat/Guns.cs's MuzzleLocal z=+3.65, Combat/Rockets.cs's pylon z=+0.9 -- the port ALREADY assumed +Z everywhere except the art)
   model_frame         localRotation = 180 deg about Y == src/planes.js's `wrapper` space, nose -Z. Every -Z-anchored measurement runs in here.
    model_scale        localScale = def.Scale == the JS's `group` (planes.js:1537); it must sit BELOW model_frame because a node's own scale does not appear in its own local space, and findCockpit measures the wrapper AFTER the scale.
     model_file        localRotation = YawUnity/RollUnity == the JS's `fixed` group (planes.js:834). Its own local space is the FILE frame, which is byte-identical to the frame PlaneProps/PropellerSystem always ran in -- which is why PROPSUM stays 31/31 with the same radii and the same hinted hubs.
      model            the FBX/OBJ at its NATURAL import transform (t28.fbx is rot (270.02,0,0) / scale 100 -- never reset).
The recentre (planes.js:830 'pivot on the AIRFRAME') is applied PRE-ROTATED to model_file.localPosition = -(fix*centre) rather than to the model, because fix*(v-c) == fix*v - fix*c but only the first leaves model_file's own origin at the FILE origin. Putting it on the model (the literal JS transcription) moved the Cessna 310's two hand-measured propHubs off their geometry and took the bake from 31 propellers to 29.

SITES HANDED THE MODEL FRAME (not sign-flipped by hand): PlaneCockpitBaker.Bake measures/builds in model_frame and converts the seat back through PlaneModelFrame.ModelPointToRoot (the frame's REAL orientation, not a hard-coded sign); PlaneCockpitKit's kit/box-shell/hood are children of model_frame so their hand-authored z offsets still mean what they say; PlaneProps via PlanePropellers.ModelRoot = model_file; PlaneHallFill measures the STRAIGHTENED box vertex-precisely (planes.js:1530's own 'precise=true' rationale -- Renderer.bounds inflates under tornado/tu144/neonfly's rotations).

units.note: STRUCTURAL, NOT A PORT — covers 0 on purpose. This is the scene component that moves the warehouse + its crane/wind tunnel + the plane hall's 35 parked aircraft off the BAKE and onto City/CityRenderer.cs's contract: nothing baked, [ExecuteAlways] OnEnable -> EnsureBuilt() regenerates from the data pipeline on every scene load. It calls exactly the same ShedFill.BuildWarehouse / Props.WarehouseCraneFill.Build / PlaneHallFill.Fill that Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs called inline, with the same arguments and the same three GAMESCENE log lines moved across verbatim, so no src/*.js behaviour is newly covered and none of shed.js/crane.js/planehall.js's remaining budget is touched. It also cannot be a CityLoader stage: City/PlaneHallRenderer.cs already calls BuildPlaneHall+Fill and its only caller is CityLoader's 'plane hall' scenery stage, and CityLoader.RunCritical/RunScenery/RunAll have NO runtime caller at all (only Editor/Probes/CityLoadProbe.cs), so a stage-only wiring renders in a probe and never in the game. ORDERING, which is load-bearing: Core/CombatWorldAdapter.Install() sweeps FindObjectsByType<PlaneDamageRecord>() exactly once, from Core/PlayableSceneBoot.Start(), and Unity delivers every OnEnable in a loading scene before any Start — so the fleet built in OnEnable is present when that sweep runs. EDITOR-ONLY AT RUNTIME, stated out loud in the class header and in its own SHEDSCENEFILL playerSafe=false log line: all three fills resolve their FBX/OBJ through AssetDatabase/PrefabUtility under #if UNITY_EDITOR, so this component builds nothing in a player build — the same limitation ParkRenderer/ShopfrontRenderer/MetroRenderer/MallRenderer/VegetationRenderer/StreetFurnitureRenderer/LandmarkRenderer all already have. A player build needs those assets reachable through Addressables or Resources; that is one change for all eight renderers and is deliberately NOT done here.

units.note: The per-instance tint shader the batch-key fix needs. Modelled on Shaders/CityWall.shader (same hand-rolled Lambert + Blinn-Phong over GetMainLight/GetAdditionalLight/SampleSH, the house choice PlaneHull.shader and WindFoliage.shader also make; same cotangent-frame TBN so no vertex TANGENT stream is needed, which the kit FBX do not carry; same _MetallicGlossMap R/A modulation; same minimal shadow caster with its OWN #pragma multi_compile_instancing, since ForwardLit's does not carry across a pass). Two deliberate differences: no vertex COLOUR read (the kit FBX have no COLOR stream and a missing stream does not reliably read as white -- the kit's tint is per INSTANCE, which is what the JS does too), and TWO multiplied colours -- _BaseColor per MATERIAL (copied off the source FBX material, where the kit's real h_plaster/a_brick/panel_concrete tones live) times _InstTint per INSTANCE. That multiply is citymap.js's instanceColor semantics (_loadAptKit's 'NO multiplyScalar here' warning against double-dimming) and it is also what lets ONE instance array serve all of a mesh's submeshes: the per-submesh colour stays on the material, so the per-instance payload is the tint alone. Every half literal carries a decimal point (the bare-integer `1h` trap that kept CityWall.shader from ever compiling, and that this same pass found twice more in PlaneHull.shader).

docs/QUALITY_BAR.md gap A: '4 painted styles and the loggia buckets fall back to a flat colour because URP's stock Lit does not sample vertex colour.' Assets/Shaders/CityWall.shader (243 lines) is a hand-rolled URP shader modelled on Assets/Shaders/PlaneHull.shader's pattern (GetMainLight/GetAdditionalLight/SampleSH rather than UniversalFragmentPBR, for the same API-stability reason PlaneHull gives) that multiplies albedo by the mesh's own vertex COLOR — the one thing BuildRich already bakes (real OSM building:colour on 40 buildings + the style chain's hue casts on thousands more) that nothing before this displayed. CityMaterials.Build() now picks CityWallShader() for EVERY wall:*/roof:* bucket (painted AND textured, not only the 4 named in the quality-bar entry) rather than switching shaders per-bucket, for one structural reason spelled out in both files' headers: BuildingBuilder.BuildRich's wall/roof meshes carry no TANGENT stream (grepped — BuildRich never calls SetTangents/RecalculateTangents, and BuildingBuilder.cs is off-limits to add it), so stock URP Lit's normal mapping would light flat/broken once Part B's real bump maps are bound. CityWall.shader sidesteps that trap entirely with a per-FRAGMENT cotangent frame built from ddx/ddy of world position and UV (the standard tangent-free normal-mapping trick) — correct lighting with zero dependency on a vertex stream BuildRich doesn't produce. pb: photo facades are untouched (stay on stock Lit via CityMaterials.LitShader()), since they carry no meaningful per-building tint and are explicitly another agent's exclusive system. CityWallShader() falls back to LitShader() if Shader.Find fails, so a shader problem degrades to the OLD flat-colour look rather than a pink/invisible building. (THREE.MeshStandardMaterial's native vertexColors — never a dedicated JS file; three.js samples mesh vertex colour for free, URP's stock Lit does not)

units.note: docs/QUALITY_BAR.md gap B, called out as 'the single biggest remaining visual gap': only albedo was ever baked for the 24 wall + 7 roof tiles (CityMaterials.cs's own prior doc comment said so outright). tools/build_tile_normals.py (311 lines, PIL 11.3.0 + numpy 2.0.2 — both already present in this environment's python3.9) derives, per tile: a tangent-space normal map from a Gaussian-blurred luminance height proxy pushed through a 3x3 Sobel gradient (edge-replicated padding, per-family depth/blur tuning — brick/stone emboss deep, plaster/panel shallow, metal modest-but-sharp), and an '_mgs.png' metallic(R)/smoothness(A) MODULATION map (both channels centred on 1.0x, derived from a local-contrast/box-blur variance measure so a busier/grimier patch of the SAME photo reads less smooth and, for metal, less uniformly metallic) — a real per-pixel roughness map, not another flat constant. Files land next to each albedo as '<stem>_n.png'/'<stem>_mgs.png' and are resolved BY FILENAME CONVENTION in CityMaterials.BindBumpAndMgs (no manifest edit needed); CityMaterials also gained MetallicFor(family) so _Metallic is no longer left at the shader's default 0 for every textured bucket. Each new PNG gets a HAND-AUTHORED Unity .meta (textureType=1/NormalMap for the _n map, textureType=0 for the _mgs map, both sRGBTexture=0 since the data is linear-encoded, never gamma-decoded) with a fresh GUID, since no agent may run the Unity editor to let AssetDatabase assign one, and a wrong default (sRGB on, Default type) would visibly break the normal map. tools/build_wall_materials.py / tools/build_roof_materials.py (the albedo-only bake this extends — no JS equivalent, three.js never had normal/roughness maps for these tiles either)
units.verified: Ran for real: `python3 tools/build_tile_normals.py` processed exactly 31/31 tiles (24 wall + 7 roof) and wrote 124 new files (31 normal PNG + 31 mgs PNG + 62 .meta). Spot-check on brick_red_n.png: R/G channel means ~127/128 (centred, i.e. real per-pixel tilt, not a flat 128 constant) with B channel mean 233.6 (mostly-upward-facing normals, consistent with a moderate emboss depth); brick_red_mgs.png R/A means ~200/213 (texture-driven variation around the 190≈1.0x baseline, not a flat uniform fill). Assets/Editor/Probes/MaterialProbe.cs id=tiles/assert_tileMapsComplete counts *.jpg vs *_n.png vs *_mgs.png in both folders via Directory.GetFiles and asserts all three equal 31 (PASS iff the Python step above has been run and its output committed) — not executed by this agent, no Unity editor access in this agent's scope; CountWithBumpMap() (CityMaterials.cs) additionally proves the maps are actually BOUND onto a real Material, not merely present on disk.

estimate._comment: Time model. These are ESTIMATES with the assumptions written down, not measurements. difficulty multiplies a system's remaining JS lines into 'effort lines'; rate_low/high are effort lines per focused hour, bracketing the uncertainty.

ui.why: UI Toolkit USS is CSS-like so the cyberpunk styling partly carries; Georgian font asset needed

estimate.rate_basis: MEASURED, not guessed. On 2026-10-26 the ported files were written between 17:06 (FlightModel.cs) and 17:59 (BuildingBuilder.cs) — 53 minutes — delivering 633 difficulty-weighted lines, i.e. ~717 effort lines/hour. That window ALSO contained the glTFast crash diagnosis, the 144-file Blender FBX conversion, editor relaunches and writing/running the verification probes, so the overhead is already inside the number. The range is 400-900: the low end is deliberately HALF the measured rate, to absorb work that is not line-translation at all (HLSL shader rewrites, bone-order debugging, perf tuning, and the 'make it feel right' tail that does not scale with line count); the high end is slightly above measured because the one-time setup — project, asset pipeline, probe harness, GeoFrame, conventions — is now done. An earlier version used 150-400, which was an unjustified haircut off this same measurement, and a 6-12 month figure, which was a solo-human-developer benchmark that does not describe how this port is actually being done.

measured.included_overhead: glTFast crash diagnosis, 144-file FBX conversion, editor restarts, probe authoring and verification runs
measured.caveat: These were the most tractable slices — self-contained maths and data parsing. The difficulty multipliers are meant to absorb the harder tail, but they are still assumptions.

parallel._comment: Hour totals are SERIAL effort-hours; work runs in parallel. critical_modules is now EMPTY, 2026-10-28. It was ['citymap','foot']: the two files judged to need one consistent head. citymap.js reached 0 lines left (8445 covered + 107 excluded of 8552), and foot.js was walked cluster-by-cluster TWICE independently -- by the Character agent and then by the budget auditor re-deriving it rather than trusting that report -- and found to have ZERO genuinely unported lines (docs/BUDGET_AUDIT.md's table: foot.js gap 393, REAL 0, already-ported ~140, no-counterpart-needed ~14, excludable 0; same for characters.js). Its 393 'free' lines are accounting slack -- `covers` under-claims what is cited and written -- not a backlog. So there is no longer an unsplittable file binding the wall-clock, and the dashboard must stop saying there is. The REAL remaining work (~240-260 lines, four UI views whose C# snapshot nothing reads) is parallelisable. NOTE this LOWERS the reported hours, which is the honest direction only because the previous number was wrong: it charged hours for work two independent walks could not find. parallel.why_these: citymap.js (8552) is the city generator whose chunk vertex ranges the damage model indexes into, and foot.js (6458) is the climb/cover/gait bone work where Unity's Animator frame order causes the qSame/freezePose class of bug. Everything else became independent once GeoFrame was proven (AxisProbe) and the mirror test existed (CityPlaceProbe), so handedness is now a written rule rather than tacit knowledge.
parallel.review_note: Verification no longer charges the critical path: a dedicated verifier agent owns the exclusive Unity project lock, compiles everything, runs every probe and diffs against the JS counterparts.

Dev-server/browser mechanics with no Unity counterpart, not unported logic. The JS fetches a body over HTTP at runtime (`/models/personages/<id>.glb`) through GLTFLoader, memoises the parsed gltf in a Map, and then SELF-HEALS a corrupt download: tools/build_characters.py rebuilds these files while the game is open, a browser that fetched one mid-write keeps serving the broken copy from its own HTTP cache, the body loads with no skinned mesh, and the personage stands there as a statue with its limbs welded on -- so hasSkeleton() detects that and refetches under `?cb=<now>`, a URL the cache has never seen (characters.js:150-156). Every link in that chain is absent in Unity: bodies are pre-converted FBX prefabs resolved by the import pipeline, there is no HTTP request, no browser cache to poison, and no cache-busting query string. Verified in the shipped code rather than assumed: CharacterRig.cs:38-39's own header records that glTFast/FBX import plus the Avatar it produces supersedes this path, and FootBelt.cs:284 records the same for _loadBody's promise chain. Only the fetch/cache/self-heal is excluded here -- pickClip() (164-178) and measureBox() (180-195) are NOT, because clip-name matching and true skinned bounds are concepts Unity does have (SkinnedMeshRenderer.bounds), so they stay in the budget.

Superseded at the IMPORTER level, not reimplemented. The file exists only to construct one shared THREE.GLTFLoader and attach a DRACOLoader to it, because in the browser a Draco-compressed .glb silently fails to parse unless a decoder is wired up first; ~45 call sites across src/ call newGltfLoader() purely to get that pre-wired loader. Unity's glTFast decompresses Draco at IMPORT time, so there is no runtime decoder-attachment step for any C# line to correspond to -- the concept, not just the implementation, is absent. Note the port does NOT runtime-load glTF at all: the 221 static GLB are imported assets and the humanoid bodies are pre-converted FBX.

A garbage-collection workaround that C# does not need. The JS keeps a module-level array of reusable THREE.Vector3 and a scope() helper that rewinds the high-water mark, because every `new THREE.Vector3()` in a per-frame physics step is a heap allocation feeding the browser's GC. Unity's Vector3 is a VALUE-TYPE struct: it lives on the stack, allocates nothing, and there is no garbage to pool against -- so PlanePhysics.cs correctly has no counterpart and never should. The absent concept is the pool, not the vectors.

One line, `if (typeof window !== 'undefined') window.__makeCharacter ??= makeCharacter;`, commented in the source itself as a "dev/tooling handle" -- it exposes the factory on the browser's global object so it can be called from the devtools console. Superseded by PhysX's own Transform/Collider coupling -- the problem this function exists to solve cannot occur in the port, traced end to end rather than assumed. In the JS, citymap's manual _addCollidable/_removeCollidable spatial hash indexes a mesh by a CACHED world-position snapshot; the slung plane moves every frame (swing + haul-up) so that snapshot goes stale and foot.js's ground probe stops finding the wing underfoot, so reindexShell re-stamps the entry every 0.15 s / 20 cm of travel. In Unity the shell is not a cached hash entry at all: Props/WarehouseCraneFill.cs:411-417 gives planeGo a plain BoxCollider on its own Transform, Props/WarehouseFanSwitch.cs:183-186 assigns that Transform's position/rotation each Update, and PhysX keeps an attached Collider in sync with its Transform for free -- there is no cache to go stale. Both readers query it live every call (WarehouseFanSwitch.RaySkinAt at :142-155, and FootController.GroundAt's Physics.Raycast with GroundMask=~0). This BoxCollider-instead-of-registration substitution is an already-documented precedent in this port, not a new liberty: Flight/PlaneHallFill.cs:208-214 calls it a deliberate UNITY-NATIVE SIMPLIFICATION of src/planehall.js's _solidify, for every other parked airframe. Decisively, City/CollidableHash<T> -- the class a literal port would have to call into -- has ZERO live instantiations (`grep -rn "new CollidableHash" unity/Assets` finds nothing), so porting reindexShell would wire a call into a system with no running instance: the exact ported-but-never-reached failure shape this project has hit fourteen times. Verified by me, not taken on trust: the grep returns empty and both cited code sites read as described.

Concept absent in Unity: a game script does not own the backbuffer or the main camera's aspect. `Camera.aspect` exists only as an OVERRIDE of the viewport-derived value -- setting it is how you deliberately diverge from the viewport, the opposite of this code's intent; there is no setSize on a camera or renderer; URP's ScriptableRenderer re-allocates its own targets on a resolution change. Re-checkable: `grep -rn "\.aspect *=\|ResetAspect()\|setSize" unity/Assets/Scripts` -> 3 hits, all deliberate off-screen render cameras (ImposterBaker, CharacterPreviewRig) plus one comment, zero on the main camera. Deliberately NOT the whole of _resize(): :2767 `this.world.setResolution(camera, renderer)` calls a concept the port kept (GameLoop.AdaptResolution, game.js:2639-2652, constants printed by CoreRestProbe) and is ALREADY-PORTED by the per-frame adaptive loop; :2759-2762 are the shell + clientWidth/Height reads that feed only these four lines, classified no-counterpart-needed.
